note: Verdicts for upstream commits touching packages this fork deleted. Regenerate with `bun scripts/check-upstream-v2-delta.mjs --update`; see scripts/check-upstream-v2-delta.mjs for the gate itself. `tracked` = accepted debt recorded in packages/kimi-agent/ROADMAP.md §6; `not-applicable` = internal refactor with no observable engine behavior to port.

entries.subject: #3717 late task settlements stay silent after session teardown
entries.note: TaskRunner gains a host-injected liveness predicate (`set_liveness_check`, v2 `taskService.lifecycleActive` / `sessionEventBus.isAgentActive`): `settle_task` gates the notification enqueue and both terminal events (`event.task.completed` / `background.task.terminated`) on it, so a settle landing after the owning session is gone announces and queues nothing. The state-bridge mirror (`persist_wire`) and the entry itself are unaffected — the task still terminates and stays queryable. Host wiring: the server answers with the session row's existence (the same check the prompt route's 404 gate uses, `HttpServer::install_task_liveness`, also re-installed on `with_task_runner` replacements); the stdio/napi hosts answer with the session handle itself — `EngineSession::is_shutdown()` plus a `Weak` sharing ownership with the session registry, so `session_dispose`'s removal is decisive. No predicate installed = the legacy always-fire behavior, so hosts that never opted in are unaffected. Tests: `settle_stays_silent_when_the_host_reports_the_session_dead`, `liveness_gate_is_per_session`, `without_a_liveness_predicate_the_settle_path_keeps_firing` (task_runner), `late_settle_for_a_deleted_session_stays_silent` (server).

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): drop the outside-working-directory access ban from the system prompt (#3879)
entries.note: The engine's own system-prompt template carried the same sentence the commit removes from v2's system.md: packages/kimi-agent/src/prompt/system.md:108 ended `Unless the user explicitly instructs otherwise, never read, write, or execute files outside the working directory.` That sentence is dropped, leaving the 'not a sandbox' framing upstream keeps. Behavior, not just a doc string: the sentence is templated into every turn's system prompt.

entries.subject: feat(agent-core-v2): support api_key_env for provider credentials (#3762)
entries.note: api_key_env for provider credentials, completed 2026-09-18: `ResolvedNativeLlm` now carries `api_key_env`, `KimiConfig::extract_native_llm` resolves the env channel (model key > model oauth > provider static key > provider oauth > provider api_key_env > unresolved), and `main.rs`'s two PipelineSpec constructors pass it to the transport, which already consumed it (`llm/http.rs:621`: env read per request, inline-key and auth_provider conflicts refused, missing/blank variable fails as `config.invalid`). Tests: `llm/http.rs` api_key_env suite (missing env, per-request reads, conflict rejection).

entries.subject: feat(agent-core-v2): approve unanalyzable bash commands in yolo permission mode (#3869)
entries.note: No counterpart state exists in this engine, so there is nothing to approve or ask about. v2's DangerousCommandAsk policy has three outcomes (dangerous / unanalyzable / no-verdict) because it feeds each Bash command through the tree-sitter bash parser, which can reject input: an unparseable command became a distinct `unanalyzable` verdict and was asked about in every mode, which is what #3869 relaxes for yolo. The fork's analyzer is `native/permission_engine/dangerous_command.rs::analyze_bash_command`, a hand-written tokenizer whose signature (`fn(&str) -> DangerousVerdict`, two variants Dangerous/Safe) cannot express a parse failure — `tokenize_command` returns `Vec<String>` with no error path — so an unrecognizable command can only fall through as Safe to the normal chain. Verified empirically rather than by reading: a temporary unit test ran ten inputs through the real function and every unparseable one (`echo 'unclosed`, `if [ -f x ]; then`, `for i in 1 2 3; do`, `$((`, `;;;`, `)))`, `` `\` ``, the empty string, and blanks) returned Safe while `sudo reboot` returned Dangerous("reboot"); the probe was then removed. Consequence: in yolo mode our engine already approves these commands (YoloModeApprove, `permission/mod.rs:440`), and in ask mode they already reach the user's normal approval decision rather than a special unanalyzable prompt — the behavior #3869 asks for, reached by a different route. No port needed.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): pre-shrink compaction history to the effective model window (#3911)
entries.note: Compaction pre-shrink (v2 `preShrinkHistoryToWindowBudget`, fullCompactionService.ts:818-841): `compaction/mod.rs` gains `summarize_with_llm_budgeted` + `pre_shrink_to_window_budget` / `take_recent_within_budget` (safety ratio 0.85, output reserve window/8, request-scaffold allowance), and `run_turn`'s overflow-recovery passes `max_context_tokens` through `force_compact_messages_with_summary_budgeted`. 3 unit tests pin fit/tail/tool-result-drop, plus the nothing-fits fallback (v2 returns an empty slice; the caller sends the original).

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): restore thinking for the openrouter reasoning dialect (#3910)
entries.note: The ported half: replayed think blocks ride the model's declared reasoning field (`[models.<alias>].reasoning_key`) instead of flattening to assistant prose (`openai.rs::project_message` now takes the key; `http.rs` passes it through). No fork equivalent of v2's `reasoning_details`-array think-part stamping exists (fork stores no detailsIndex), so the string-vs-details coexistence case keeps the string, which the fork already read. Regression test pins both shapes.

entries.subject: feat: expose resolved base_url on models.dev catalog provider items (#3909)
entries.note: `base_url` now rides every `/api/v1/catalog/providers` item (resolved endpoint per built-in entry; the fork serves a built-in list, not a models.dev proxy, so the endpoint is stated rather than resolved), the per-id route reads the same shared source instead of fabricating a placeholder (unknown id = 404), and server-api.md documents the new field. Matches the v2 item shape (`modelsDevImport.ts` `ModelsDevProviderItem.base_url`).

entries.subject: feat(kimi-code): carry turn trace id and copilot stats in rating surveys (#3907)
entries.note: Survey trace id + copilot stats: the engine `turn_ended` telemetry payload now carries `trace_id` (engine-minted `turn-<id>`; a provider request id is still not visible to the engine, noted in wire-schema.ts), `TurnEndedEvent` gains an optional `traceId` (interface + zod) passed through the napi bridge, and the survey controller records `kfc_trace_id` plus `subagent_count`/`subagent_models`/`swarm_run_count`/`swarm_models` per turn. `tower_mode_enter/exit` emit from the SDK `setTowerMode` flip point, where the flag actually lives.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): reuse the queued prompt id for a single steer (#3906)
entries.note: Steer identity end to end: `LLMMessage.prompt_id` (new optional field, persisted as a `messages.prompt_id` column with the store's idempotent ALTER pattern), `ServerEngine::enqueue_steer` mints an id when the caller sent none, the REST `prompt_ids` steer route reuses the queued prompt's own id (v2 `children[0].waiter.id`), and the v3 projection keeps a steered user message inside the current turn under that id with `origin.inTurn = true` (v2 `markInTurnOrigin`) instead of minting a turn of its own. `translate_wire_event` applies the same rule live. 2 projection tests pin in-turn placement and the no-open-turn fallback.

entries.subject: feat: add usage telemetry for swarm, tower, external hooks, and remote control (#3897)
entries.note: Telemetry emissions: `swarm_mode_entered/exited` on the profile-write transition, `external_hook_resolved` in `HookGuard::denial` (action/matched_count/failed_count, verdict untouched) riding `HostCallbacks::telemetry` via a OnceLock sink, `remote_control_toggle` with v2 outcome vocabulary on the REST route. Server routes without a host callback fall back to `tracing::info` via `HttpServer::emit_session_telemetry` (`with_telemetry_sink` for host integration). Only `tower_mode_enter/exit` remains: tower mode has no engine-side flip point yet.

entries.subject: fix(transcript): attach promptIds to cold-folded steer frames (#3896)
entries.note: v2 synthesizes cold-rebuilt transcript frames after reload, so a steered frame needed its promptIds re-attached. The fork's engine persists steered user messages as real messages in the sqlite history and its transcript projection (server/transcript/*) reads them back from the store — there is no cold-fold synthesis path to lose the linkage in. packages/transcript itself is a live fork-kept package and takes upstream changes via normal merges.

entries.subject: feat(agent-core-v2): make select_tools failures actionable (#3885)
entries.note: tools/select_tools.rs gains the already-callable classification (advertised minus deferred → direct-call guidance, not an error), suggest_tool_names (case-fix, mcp__-stripped substring, last __ segment; sorted, capped at 3), the loadable-count-based unknown guidance arms, and the new description/announcement wording. The dispatch arm computes the callable set as the full catalogue minus deferred_tool_names_blocking. Loadable lists render sorted (a Rust HashSet has no insertion order to inherit). Tests: evaluate/suggest/lifecycle suites extended.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): drop literal decision clauses from system prompt and auto reminder (#3894)
entries.note: Both upstream-aligned texts applied: prompt/system.md 'Delivering work' paragraph and injection/permission_mode.rs AUTO_ENTER_REMINDER AskUserQuestion line ('decide and continue.'). The fork's AutoModeAskUserQuestionDeny message is fork-authored ('Auto mode cannot ask interactive questions'), not the upstream string, and stays. permission_mode 8 tests and prompt 33 tests pass.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): stop workspace watchers from listing a flooded project root (#3892)
entries.note: The fixed failure mode is v2's OS directory watcher inventorying a project root into the V8 heap. The fork's fs_watch (server/fs_watch.rs) is mtime polling of explicitly registered file paths — there is no root watch, no directory-tree listing, and nothing that can flood a heap on a pathological root. The [watch] enabled kill switch has no fork counterpart because there is no watcher subsystem to disable; if a kill switch is ever wanted it belongs on the fs_watch registry, recorded here for that future.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): keep session deletion from hanging (#3887)
entries.note: All three hang mechanisms are v2-lifecycle-internal: (1) AgentLifecycleService.remove awaiting loop.settled past its quiesce deadline, (2) setSessionArchived awaiting a pending resume inside the lifecycle critical section, (3) an unbounded taskkill wait. The fork's delete route (server/mod.rs :4107) reads the row, deletes via the store, cancels interactions, fires SessionEnd hooks and publishes event.session.deleted — there is no lifecycle chain to wedge and no settle await to bound. The compaction-after-abort guard (signal check between summary return and apply) the fork already has: summarize_with_llm re-checks the CancellationToken immediately after the chat await returns, before any apply.

entries.subject: perf: speed up session resume and session index on large workspaces (#3889)
entries.note: The optimized layers (wire restore single-pass, immer freeze deferral, kap-server incremental wire cache, O(1) by-id session index, dir-mtime freshness) are all v2/kap-server architecture the fork does not have: session restore is a direct SQLite read (session/sqlite_store.rs), the session index is table lookups, and there is no immer/wire-restore replay path. Nothing to port; the fork's equivalent hot paths have a different shape entirely.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): stop advertising unregistered tools and clarify Read media errors (#3878)
entries.note: Half 1 (invariant): `every_advertised_builtin_tool_is_resolvable` in `tools/agent_tool.rs` pins that every builtin profile's advertised tool name resolves (`is_native_tool_name`) and passes its own `ToolPolicyFilter` gate — the listing and the gate share one source, so the class of bug upstream fixed cannot occur. Half 2 (Read media wording): verified against v2 by diff — the three limit messages (`delivery_limit_error` / `decode_limit_error` / `full_resolution_limit_error`) match `buildImageDeliveryLimitError` / `buildImageDecodeLimitError` / `buildFullResolutionLimitError` word for word, differing only in the tool name (`Read`, not `ReadMediaFile`), which is correct because the fork has no separate media tool — media rides `Read` itself (`tool-name-contract.json`); the capability-gated refusal names the file kind and the missing `image_in`/`video_in` capability per v2, so the `ReadMediaFile`-pointer variant is not applicable.

entries.subject: fix(agent-core-v2): pair steered follow-ups by reserved message id (#3891)
entries.note: The steered-message identity the pairing needs now exists: the persisted `prompt_id` rides history reload, the v3 projection emits the steered user under its prompt id with an in-turn origin, and the live translator mirrors both — so a client can pair a steered follow-up to its reserved prompt id instead of matching by content. (v2's `steeredMessageIds` join lives in `packages/transcript`, which has no fork consumer; the equivalent information now travels on the v3 entities.)
